parts.t: RECIPE 09 — Plan mode 90% of the time, and gates on your words
From: How I Get 30M+ Monthly Views with Claude Code + Blotato · 17 Feb 2026 · 1:12:20 · watch

**She calls it her "ultimate Claude Code free course", built on "over 500 hours using Claude Code on a regular basis." The Blotato half you can skip. The Claude Code half is the most useful hour of the twelve.**
THE ONE THING — plan mode, 90% of the time
"I spend about 90% of my time in plan mode so that Claude doesn't accidentally change anything. And then when I'm very happy with a plan, then I switch to edit automatically.
" "we spend 90% of our time back and forth sparring back and forth on the plan. And then only when I'm super happy with it and confident it's going to not break stuff, then I switch."
Why this matters more to you than to almost anyone
Your usage report, measured this week:
Plan mode is the mechanical answer to exactly that. It is a switch at the bottom left that stops me touching anything until you have agreed what I am about to do.
She does add one caveat: for a small build from scratch you can be "a little more aggressive". Her 90% figure is for complex existing work — which is what yours is.
The second thing: quality gates on CONTENT, not just process
"we can have Claude Code automatically check every single post for em dashes, remove them or replace them before they get published.
" "you can also think about keywords that your brand doesn't want to be associated with. You can also think about colour schemes in the visuals."
You already have hooks. You already have 174 product gates. You have nothing checking your words.
PDF page counts
listing titles
Image resolution
descriptions
Corridor widths
anything you write
Recipe 04 found the same gap from a different video. Two of her videos, independently, point at the same hole in your setup.
The permissions advice — and how it fits today's audit
She gives a prompt that grants Claude the boring commands so it stops asking:
"it will tell Claude Code to allow most relatively safe commands. By safe, I mean non-destructive commands so that it doesn't ask you again and again." "it's checking what's in a directory...
you're not going to break anything."
Put that beside what your reviewers said today
Neither half is the whole answer. Both at once is.
And she is explicit about the limit: "It's more about your familiarity with it. Do you know what Claude Code is doing? Are you able to follow along?"
Her plan advice — worth knowing before your next bill
"I am personally on the $200 per month plan...
If you are just on the $20 per month plan, you are going to hit the limits very quickly because of all the tool calls involved when you use an agentic tool like Claude Code.
So I recommend at minimum this $100 per month plan."
And her honest counterweight: "you will find that you will be able to cancel so many different tools once you actually pick up Claude Code."
That is money, so it is yours. I am reporting her figures, not recommending a plan.
One habit she ends the course with

"your memory as you do these projects — adding them to your CLAUDE.md, the things you've learned, tips and tricks that are helpful... make sure to add that to your CLAUDE.md at the end of every session."
You do this already, heavily. But note what she says it is FOR: things learned, not rules imposed. Your file has drifted toward the second.
What to try — one switch, tonight
That costs nothing, needs no setup, and is aimed straight at the thing your own usage report says annoys you most.

a week's worth of content, including visuals, show you the plan so you can edit it... wait for your approval, and then schedule everything"*

review the work that Claude Code is doing"*
